tldr: Typed decision models return a probability over caller-defined options instead of generating text, and papers started placing them in agent systems. A perimeter-triage study and an inbox-routing comparison against classical and generative baselines came first.
whats_new: A controlled audit finds typed decision models, including Jev, Clef Flash and Perplexity Decider, are sensitive to how the evaluated text is presented in subjective evaluation.
why_it_matters: If a typed decision model gates actions or scores outputs, formatting changes alone can shift its decisions, so the gate needs its own robustness tests.

status.detail: Three papers in 14 days move from application and baseline comparison to a robustness audit of typed decision models.

beats.headline: Typed, calibrated heads for perimeter triage
Measuring typed models against classical and generative baselines
Audit finds sensitivity to presentation in subjective evaluation

open_questions: Do typed decision models hold their advantage over classical baselines on other routing tasks?
Do vendors publish mitigations or presentation-invariance guarantees for typed decision models?
take_for_builders: Before a typed decision model gates agent actions or grades outputs, rerun your eval with reformatted inputs and compare against a classical baseline.
